# Results — Study 853 (Days-Sales-Outstanding Buildup)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **a rising
Days Sales Outstanding (receivables growing faster than sales) is a red flag that precedes weaker
future sales and lower returns** (Abarbanell-Bushee). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Prices fingerprint `83a4ccfa2027` (yfinance
daily adjusted closes); events cache = 1,173 (ticker, filing) rows.*

**Fingerprint `83a4ccfa2027`** · as-of **2026-06-30** · 38 names · 191 long-short months.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | **38** large US filers (of a 48-name basket) with matched receivables + revenue history on EDGAR (fixed, current survivors; financials excluded — DSO is undefined for them) |
| Signal source | SEC EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept`: `AccountsReceivableNetCurrent` (→ `ReceivablesNetCurrent`) and quarterly `Revenues` (→ `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax`), longest per-name history; de-duplicated on period end, earliest filing kept |
| Panel | **1,173** receivables quarters, period ends **2009-07-31 → 2026-04-30**, stamped with the **10-Q/10-K filing date** (point-in-time; no look-ahead) |
| Prices | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, 47 names, sliced to 2026-06-30 |
| Primary signal | `dso_yoy_chg` = DSO(quarter) − DSO(same quarter a year earlier), in days, where DSO = AR ÷ (annualised quarterly revenue ÷ 365). Ranked on `dso_score = −dso_yoy_chg` (high = lean = long) |
| Primary test | calendar-time monthly long-short: rank fresh signals into **terciles**, **long the lean (low-buildup) third / short the building (high-buildup) third**, earn **next** month's return (one execution lag); decisive stat = **Newey-West (6-lag) t** |
| Costs | one-way × NAV × monthly turnover on both legs + annualised borrow on the short leg |

**Coverage caveat (first-class).** The matched (receivables, revenue) cross-section actually
**shrinks** over the sample — ≈27 names early (pre-2013) down to ≈12 by the mid-2020s — as the
ASC-606 (2018) revenue-tag switches break the same-fiscal-quarter YoY revenue match for several
names. Terciles on a thin cross-section are noisy by construction. No survivorship correction: the
basket is current survivors — named on the Signal axis.

## Headline — the forward-return long-short (does DSO buildup predict returns?)

Monthly rebalanced tercile long-short on `dso_score` (long lean / short building), one execution
lag, 2010-08 → 2026-06 (**191 months**, avg cross-section 21.4 names):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| long-short mean | **+14.2 bps/month** (+1.71%/yr, gross) |
| one-sample *t* | +0.55 |
| **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** | **+0.53** |
| Sharpe (gross, ann.) | 0.14 |
| monthly hit rate | 52% (Wilson 95% CI [45%, 59%]) |
| long leg / short leg | +148.6 / +134.3 bps/month |
| growth of \$1 (gross) | ×1.16 over 191 months |

The point estimate is **right-signed** (lean names beat building names, as the red flag predicts)
but **economically trivial and statistically indistinguishable from zero** (NW *t* = +0.53). It
does not survive perturbation: a **staleness-120** variant collapses to +4.8 bps (NW *t* = +0.16),
and the unit-free **percentage-change** signal `ΔDSO/DSO` is +6.6 bps (NW *t* = +0.27, Sharpe
0.06). There is no certifiable return predictability here.

## Cross-check — pooled event drift (tercile sort by signed score)

Bucket all (ticker, filing) events by `dso_score`; top-minus-bottom (lean-minus-building) forward
drift, entered one day after the filing:

| horizon | n | top (lean) | bottom (building) | long-short | one-sample *t* | win | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 d (≈1 m) | 1,172 | +1.31% | +1.30% | **+0.01%** | +0.01 | 50% | 0.49 |
| 63 d (≈1 q) | 1,163 | +4.43% | +4.32% | **+0.11%** | +0.11 | 51% | 0.44 |
| 126 d (≈2 q) | 1,157 | +8.10% | +9.12% | **−1.01%** | −0.74 | 50% | 0.81 |

Flat, and the sign **flips with the horizon** (the building third out-returns the lean one over two
quarters). The 63d tercile means are **non-monotone** (+4.32% / +3.55% / +4.43%, building→lean),
the long-short *t* never exceeds +0.11 on the claimed side, and the label-shuffle placebo *p* runs
0.44-0.81 — a random tercile split matches or beats the real one. A horizon-dependent sign is the
signature of noise, not a signal.

## Era split — no regime rescues it

Calendar long-short, split at 2018-01-01 (the ASC-606 revenue-tagging break):

| era | months | mean | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2010-2017 | 89 | +29.8 bps | +1.03 |
| 2018-2026 | 102 | +0.7 bps | +0.02 |

What little full-sample positive exists lives **entirely before 2018** (and even there falls short
of the bar at *t* = +1.03); after 2018 it is **stone dead** (+0.7 bps, *t* = +0.02). The modern
half is both thinner (cross-section shrinks) and flatter. There is no era in which the signal
certifies.

## The mechanism — a building DSO warns on future sales only **faintly**

Pooled OLS of **next quarter's** YoY revenue growth on this quarter's DSO change (winsorised at
1/99% to remove a handful of near-zero-prior-revenue YoY artefacts; n = 997 matched events):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| slope *b* | **−0.0031** (correctly negative) |
| *t* (iid-pooled) | −2.67 |
| R² | 0.007 |
| Pearson correlation | **−0.084** |
| future sales growth, lean-DSO tercile | **+8.2%** |
| future sales growth, building-DSO tercile | **+4.9%** |
| tercile spread (lean − building) | **+3.3 pp** |

The channel-stuffing mechanism is **present in the sign** — lean-DSO names grow next quarter's
sales +3.3 percentage points faster than building-DSO names, and the slope is correctly negative —
but **negligible in magnitude** (correlation −0.08, R² 0.007). The pooled *t* clears 2 only because
n is large and clustered; read the magnitude. This is the study's *strongest* result and it is a
whisper. (Unlike a signal that leads its fundamental cleanly, here the "red flag" barely moves even
the number it is built from.)

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic price + signal panel with a TUNABLE planted red flag (building-DSO names drift down);
no network. Detector = the primary calendar long-short NW *t*.

| world | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **12 seeds** | mean **+0.01** (sd 0.73), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **0/12** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.15 (seed 853) | **+18.51** (mean +860.8 bps/month) |

The detector averages ≈0 on the null (zero crossings in twelve HAC *t*'s) and lights up hard on a
planted red flag. The real-tape NW *t* = +0.53 is therefore a genuine null, not a broken pipeline.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of a real-tape stamp.)*

## Tradability — the timer

Calendar long-short net of one-way costs × turnover (both legs) + short-leg borrow (monthly
turnover ≈ 0.17):

| cost (one-way) | borrow (ann.) | net mean | ~ann. | Newey-West *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | 50 bps | +6.6 bps/mo | +0.79%/yr | +0.25 | 0.06 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps | −1.0 bps/mo | −0.13%/yr | −0.04 | −0.01 |

The gross edge was already indistinguishable from zero; realistic friction tips the net return
**negative**. You cannot get paid for a spread you cannot certify.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The forward-return long-short is right-signed but **statistically zero**
  (primary NW *t* = +0.53, one-sample +0.55), it does **not** survive perturbation (staleness-120
  *t* = +0.16, percentage-change *t* = +0.27), the pooled event drift is **flat and sign-flipping**
  (long-short *t* +0.01 → +0.11 → −0.74; placebo *p* 0.44-0.81), and it is **dead post-2018**
  (*t* = +0.02). No coherent, robust effect — the desk's `NONE`. (One execution lag; survivorship
  named on the Signal axis; as-of 2026-06-30.)
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Not certifiable even gross; net of realistic long-short costs + borrow
  it is **negative** (−0.13%/yr, *t* = −0.04). No paycheck.
- **"Does a building DSO warn on future sales?" — FAINT.** The mechanism is correctly signed
  (slope −0.0031, +3.3 pp lean-minus-building future-sales spread) but economically negligible
  (correlation −0.08). Real in direction, a whisper in size — not the lead the red flag promises.

> On big, liquid, heavily-covered names, a rising DSO is a real-but-tiny hint about next quarter's
> sales and — as far as this tape can tell — no hint at all about the stock.
